lines.text: $f$ is injective only if $\hl{1}{f(a) = f(b)}$ forces $\hl{2}{a = b}$. Set $\hl{1}{f(b) = 5}$.

steps.ask: Which of the two values of b is different from 0?
steps.title: Choose the value other than 0

lines.text: Since $\hl{2}{b \neq 0}$, $\hl{2}{b = 6}$. Then $\hl{1}{f(6)} = 36 - 36 + 5 = 5 = \hl{1}{f(0)}$ with $6 \neq 0$, so $f$ is not injective.

problems.note: This is an arrow diagram, so the checks are read off the arrows instead of solved, and part (i) first asks for g(f(3)). The injective check (no two inputs share an output) is the idea from problems 1 and 2; the not-surjective check (an output that no arrow reaches) is new.

steps.ask: Which element does f send 3 to, and where does g send that element?
steps.title: (i) Follow 3 through f, then through g

lines.text: In the diagram, $f$ sends $3$ to the globe.
$g$ sends the globe to $\hl{1}{w}$.

steps.ask: Do any two different elements of B go to the same element of C?
steps.title: (ii) Show g is injective (one-to-one)

lines.text: The three elements of $B$ (plane, globe, cloud) go to three different elements of $C$: $\hl{1}{x}$, $\hl{1}{w}$ and $\hl{1}{z}$.
No element of $C$ is used more than once, so $g$ is injective.

steps.ask: Is there an element of C that no arrow reaches?
steps.title: (ii) Show g is not surjective (not onto)

lines.text: The element $\hl{1}{y}$ in $C$ has no arrow pointing to it.
So the range $\{\hl{1}{x}, \hl{1}{w}, \hl{1}{z}\}$ is not all of $C$, and $g$ is not surjective.
